title: The rules changed as a sign company reapplied for 35 permits

beats.text: On the same day San Francisco approved a sign settlement, two supervisors proposed changing the rules.

visual.sub: The Board approved a settlement and introduced a rule on the same day

beats.text: The company had 270 days to apply for permits.

visual.kicker: The Board approved a settlement and introduced a rule on the same day

beats.text: The new rule limited space for advertising that was secondary to the store’s business.
The company applied for its 35 signs. The City denied them.

visual.label: The court identified what happened to the 35 applications

beats.text: Some signs also had other problems, according to the court.

visual.kicker: The court identified what happened to the 35 applications

beats.text: The court held that the rules at the time of permitting applied.

visual.line: Rules at the time of permitting

beats.text: The 2019 attorney fee settlement called for $500,000.

visual.kicker: The second attorney-fee ordinance expressly changed the first

beats.text: The revised agreement called for $580,000, including money already in escrow.
The remaining amount was divided into 12 monthly installments.

visual.kicker: The second attorney-fee ordinance expressly changed the first

beats.text: A separate 2020 sign application names the same company as lessee.

visual.kicker: A later public permit still had no issue date

beats.text: After 2,507 days, its public record still had no issue date.

visual.label: A later public permit still had no issue date

beats.text: The record does not say who was responsible for the delay.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
